title: Tenant-aware hybrid experiment controller for shadowing and auto-heal
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a controller that enables tenant-scoped hybrid experiments across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments: - Support tenant-scoped A/B and canary exposures (percent-based and token-based splits) - Controlled shadowing with selective sampling and privacy-safe telemetry collection - Automatic rollback/auto-heal based on configurable metric windows and anomaly detectors - Environment-specific translation layer to map a single experiment spec to Hosted/Dedicated/Private constraints (networking, telemetry endpoints, max batch sizes, KV cache behavior, and RBAC) The controller should be runtime-agnostic, produce canonical experiment events for the Console and Optimize, and provide hooks for SRE-runbooks and emergency kill-switches.
acceptance_criteria: A single Experiment YAML can be applied and creates equivalent exposed behavior on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private targets (where supported).
Shadow traffic can be enabled per-tenant with sampling rate, and shadowed requests are routed to a sandbox model endpoint without affecting production response paths.
Auto-rollback triggers when metrics cross configured thresholds (latency P95 + error rate) for N consecutive windows and triggers a rollback action verified in staging before production promotion.
Console shows per-tenant experiment breakdown, traffic splits, observed deltas (latency/cost/quality) and a prominent kill-switch to immediately stop experiment traffic.
Experiment controller enforces environment constraints: e.g., no cross-VPC telemetry by default for Private, and batch-size ceilings for small Dedicated pools.
End-to-end integration tests simulate mixed tenant load across modes and validate that canary percentages converge to expected rates within 1% over 10 minutes.
Security review completed and KMS/HSM keys referenced for telemetry and audit logs in Private deployments.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff — scoped experiment spec format, initial schema drafted and reviewed with PM and Design (doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DEP/Hybrid+Experiment+Spec).
2026-02-22: Prototype routing adapter implemented for Hosted -> sandbox endpoint. Local demo validated with synthetic traffic harness (tests/poc/shadow_harness).
2026-02-28: Environment translation layer prototype completed — maps canonical spec to Dedicated config (batch ceilings, autoscale hints).

2026-03-03: First integration tests failing intermittently due to KV cache warmup differences in Dedicated; added warmup hook to controller (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4829).
2026-03-08: Safety review meeting — agreed on default conservative sampling for shadowing in Private and mandatory security_review flag on experiment creation.
2026-03-10: Implemented auto-rollback evaluator and anomaly detector thresholds; running long-duration chaos tests in staging.
comments: PM (Emily Chen): Prioritize tenant-scope and visibility for Console — our customers need per-tenant delta metrics for billing and quality tracking.
Design (Carlos Nguyen): UX needs explicit distinctions between shadow vs mirrored traffic; propose separate telemetry channels and clearer labeling in Console.
SRE (Marta Ivanov): Add an emergency global kill endpoint that can be executed by oncall; ensure the rollback also triggers tenant-specific cache invalidation where relevant.
Engineering (Luca Moretti): Noted constraint — Private deployments cannot call hosted telemetry collectors; solution: buffered telemetry to local S3 or customer-provided endpoint.
test_plan: Unit tests for spec translation logic (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private).
Integration test: simulated tenants with mixed mode traffic validating split ratios over time window.
Chaos test: forced host endpoint failures to assert fallback and rollback behaviors.
Security test: verify no telemetry egress from Private by default; KMS key rotation dry run.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary staging): enable controller for internal tenants only; monitor Console deltas for 48h.
Phase 1 (early customers): opt-in for selected customers on Hosted; collect feedback and iterate metrics.
Phase 2 (Dedicated): enable translation layer and restrict batch sizes; run with 5 pilot tenants.
Phase 3 (Private): deliver controller as opt-in operator with sandboxed telemetry sinks and documented install steps.
Fallback: global kill-switch and per-tenant emergency stop documented in runbook (runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Experiment+Runbook).
tradeoffs: Complexity vs parity: maintaining exact runtime parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private is infeasible. We opt for a canonical spec + environment translators to favor developer ergonomics over perfect behavioral parity.
Telemetry fidelity vs privacy: Private deployments will default to lower-fidelity telemetry and local buffering; this reduces observability but preserves privacy constraints.
Performance vs safety: conservative default sampling for shadowing increases time-to-signal but reduces blast radius; customers can opt-in to higher sampling after review.
next_steps: Stabilize KV cache warmup hook and add tenant TTL mapping for Dedicated pools.
Finish security review and add automated KMS binding for Private telemetry sinks.
Merge PRs and schedule Phase 0 canary for internal tenants on 2026-03-20.
Prepare Console UX updates for experiment detail page and add kill-switch button behind feature flag.
